Here’s what I found for the most recent Python 3.12 release notes: **Title:** Python 3.12 Release Notes **Source:** https://docs.python.org/3.12/whatsnew/3.12.html **Key highlights from the notes:** | Feature / Improvement | Description | |-----------------------|-------------| | **Isolated Sub‑interpreters** | New API to create truly isolated sub‑interpreters, improving concurrency and sandboxing. | | **Enhanced Error Messages** | More precise syntax‑error locations, clearer tracebacks, and better suggestions for common mistakes. | | **Performance Boosts** | Optimizations in the interpreter core, faster startup, and reduced memory usage. | | **Linux perf Profiling Support** | Direct integration with Linux `perf` for low‑overhead profiling of Python code. | | **Pattern Matching Enhancements** | Expanded capabilities for structural pattern matching, including guard expressions and more flexible case handling. | | **TypedDict & typing improvements** | New syntax for required/optional keys, better static analysis support. | | **Standard Library Updates** | • `zoneinfo` now supports IANA time‑zone database updates automatically.
• `asyncio` got new debugging utilities.
• `statistics` added `fmean` for floating‑point means.
• Numerous deprecations and removals of legacy modules. | | **Security Fixes** | Updated OpenSSL bindings, tightened SSL/TLS defaults, and patched several CVEs. | | **Documentation & Tooling** | Updated “What’s New” guide, improved Sphinx documentation theme, and new `python -X` command‑line options for experimental features. | You can read the full release notes on the official Python documentation site at the link above. If you need a deeper dive into any specific section (e.g., the new sub‑interpreter API or the enhanced error messages), just let me know!
